name: cpu_llm_infer

license.notes: Task source stays source-available; llama.cpp is MIT and the Qwen2.5 model weights are Apache-2.0 (both permissive), so neither imposes copyleft.

libraries.name: llama.cpp
libraries.usage: Loads the bundled GGUF model and runs it on the CPU through ggml; the greedy token generation loop (one llama_process call per token) is the measured workload.
libraries.notes: Built from the pinned submodule without source modifications. llama, ggml and ggml-base are shared libraries and every CPU ISA variant is a separate ggml-cpu backend module (GGML_BACKEND_DL with GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS); all of them ship next to the task in both build modes and the task loads the best CPU module at runtime. Includes llamafile's sgemm (MIT, Mozilla Foundation).

libraries.name: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (GGUF, Q4_K_M)
libraries.usage: The language model whose weights the measured generation loop streams and multiplies (qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf).
libraries.notes: Downloaded at build time from the pinned revision and verified by SHA256; redistributed unmodified.

title: Local language model on CPU
short_description: Token generation from a small quantised language model on the CPU.

structured_text.description: Generates text from Qwen2.5 0.5B, a small language model quantised to 4 bits, running entirely on the processor, the way local assistants run on machines without a capable GPU. The model, prompt and greedy decoding are fixed, and the work is largely bound by how fast the CPU can move and multiply the model weights.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the number of tokens generated per second during steady output, reported in tokens per second.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. More tokens per second means a more responsive local assistant, since text appears closer to reading speed.
structured_text.reasoning: Running language models locally is now a mainstream use, and CPU inference is bound by memory bandwidth and vector math in a way that reflects real assistant performance.
